name: 3D Interaction Intent System
purpose: Prevent visually impressive but semantically wrong 3D interactions by matching subject structure, user goal, camera behaviour and technical implementation before scene design.
hardRules: Never choose an interaction because it is impressive; choose it because it explains, inspects, configures, compares, navigates or tells a verified story about the subject.

A subject must support the proposed motion physically or conceptually. Assembly requires meaningful separable parts; exploded view requires real component hierarchy; walkthrough requires navigable spatial geometry; material switching requires real variants.
Camera motion must serve the task. Zoom, orbit, dolly, truck, pan, crane, fly-through and first-person navigation are not interchangeable effects.
Do not animate a real product, property or mechanism in ways that imply capabilities, geometry or construction that are not verified.
For scroll-driven scenes, define authored camera states and semantic chapters before interpolation.
For direct manipulation, preserve stable orientation, bounded controls, reset/recenter and keyboard/DOM alternatives.
When a still, video or CSS treatment communicates the same information more clearly, prefer the simpler medium.
Every interaction must have reduced-motion and non-WebGL fallbacks that preserve the primary information and action.

reject: free first-person navigation around a small product
parts forming from arbitrary particles when the product has no meaningful assembly story
unbounded orbit that loses product orientation
vehicle interactions on unrelated businesses
fake drivetrain internals
impossible deformation presented as product behaviour
continuous spinning as the primary experience

cameraLanguage: exterior orbit only when site context matters
requirements: verified spatial geometry or clearly labelled concept model
reject: house parts flying together unless construction sequence is the actual story
unverified rooms or amenities
camera paths that pass through solid walls without an intentional section transition
free-flight controls when a guided property tour is clearer

requirements: real variant evidence for fabric switching
reject: mechanical exploded view of a garment without a construction purpose
automotive-style assembly choreography
fabric physics implying material properties that are not known
industrial exploded view language
unrelated mechanical assembly
ingredients or toppings not actually offered
decorative globe with fake routes
particle motion that is not mapped to data
3D depth that makes values harder to compare
generic premium geometry with no mapping
random liquid/refraction spectacle
abstract object that could be reused unchanged for any industry

cameraOperations.zoom: Change lens field-of-view. Use sparingly because it changes perspective compression and can feel unnatural.
cameraOperations.dolly-in-out: Move camera toward or away from the subject. Preferred for cinematic approach/reveal and property movement when spatial relationship matters.
cameraOperations.orbit: Rotate camera around a stable target. Use for inspection of bounded objects, not as a default website effect.
cameraOperations.pan-tilt: Rotate camera from a fixed position. Use to redirect attention without changing position.
cameraOperations.truck-pedestal: Translate camera laterally or vertically. Useful for silhouette, architecture and spatial reveal.
cameraOperations.fly-through: Translate through a navigable environment. Appropriate for property, spatial worlds and verified digital twins, with collision/bounds and guided alternatives.
cameraOperations.target-focus: Interpolate camera and target to a labelled detail. Appropriate for components, rooms, amenities and hotspots.
cameraOperations.section-transition: Coordinate clipping/section planes with camera movement to reveal interiors or layers. Requires meaningful internal structure.

limits: harder to adapt to user-controlled viewpoint
complex custom logic may outgrow tool
